speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin, could you tell me how long you have noticed this neck swelling and whether it is painful or tender to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of colon cancer, I need to rule out metastasis, so REQUEST TEST: CT scan of the neck and REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of the neck mass. Additionally, has the mass changed in size or texture, and have you experienced any unintended weight loss or night sweats?

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CT and biopsy are reassuring against metastasis or infection, but the location on the nape is specific. Do you have any skin changes like hyperpigmentation or thickening in that area, and does the swelling feel rubbery or fixed to the underlying tissue?

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying your medications. Given the location on the nape, the rubbery consistency, and the absence of systemic symptoms or malignancy on biopsy, this presentation is highly characteristic of a benign soft tissue tumor. DIAGNOSIS READY: Lipoma
